question: How many times faster is delamination at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C, and what is that boiling point?
rendered:
According to the text, delamination takes around 2 seconds at the boiling point of ethylene glycol, and around 6 seconds at 160 °C.

To calculate how many times faster delamination is at the boiling point of ethylene glycol, we can divide the time it takes at 160 °C by the time it takes at the boiling point:

6 seconds (at 160 °C) ÷ 2 seconds (at boiling point) = 3

So, delamination at the boiling point of ethylene glycol is 3 times faster than at 160 °C.

The boiling point of ethylene glycol is 198 °C.
